bibl.title: Dynamics of social representation in the mouse prefrontal cortex

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: existence
span.quote: Here, we show that neurons in the medial PFC (mPFC) of freely behaving mice preferentially respond to socially-relevant sensory cues.

span.label: social representation in medial prefrontal cortex
span.quote: We studied the representation of social information in the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) of freely-behaving mice.

span.label: electrophysiology
span.quote: We recorded stimulus-evoked responses of mPFC units (n = 194; 6 mice) and found that 44% responded to at least one stimulus, typically by increasing their firing rates (Fig. 2a and Supplementary Fig. 2a-c).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Elevated baseline cortical noise degrades the mPFC's ability to form category-specific social representations and to drive the synaptic plasticity that refines them
span.quote: The strong negative correlation we observe between baseline noise and social category representations suggests that noise plays an important role in the failure of mPFC activity in Cntnap2-/- mice to appropriately represent social stimuli and drive synaptic plasticity processes.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Loss of CNTNAP2 impairs targeting of AMPA and NMDA receptors to post-synaptic membranes, removing the plasticity that would otherwise refine odour-category representations with experience
span.quote: The loss of experience-based refinement of odor category representation in Cntnap2-/- mice might be linked with the role of CNTNAP2 protein in targeting AMPA and NMDA receptors to post-synaptic membranes78,79.

span.label: The social/nonsocial distinction is a distinction between two sets of odours.
span.note: what this limits: any claim that this mPFC activity encodes social information: the tuning measure is the normalised odor-evoked response magnitude, and it was higher for male and female cues than for all nonsocial odors
span.quote: The average unit tuning, calculated as the normalized odor-evoked response magnitude in all units that showed stimulus-associated responses, was higher for both male and female cues than for all nonsocial odors, regardless of odor identity

span.label: Two of the three behavioural measures did not differ between social and nonsocial stimuli.
span.note: what this limits: any behavioural evidence that the mice treated social cues differently: orientation probability was higher for social cues, while response latency and the stimulus-evoked increase in locomotion did not significantly differ
span.quote: The probability of odor-directed orientation responses was higher during delivery of social cues (Fig. 1c). However, the response latency (Fig. 1d) and the stimulus-evoked increase in locomotion (Fig. 1e) did not significantly differ between social and nonsocial stimuli

span.label: The paper's central quantity is a log ratio of distances between activity patterns.
span.note: what this limits: any social distinction index quoted from this work: it was calculated to quantify the separation between the representations of social and nonsocial stimuli for each mouse
span.quote: To quantify the separation between representation of social (S) and nonsocial (NS) stimuli for each mouse, we calculated a social distinction index

span.label: baseline firing rate and locomotion as explanations for the elevated noise
span.quote: Multiple regression analysis revealed that the elevated baseline noise levels in Cntnap2-/- mice could not be linearly predicted by either elevated baseline unit firing rates, nor by behavioral locomotion levels

span.label: social distinction index
span.quote: To quantify the separation between representation of social (S) and nonsocial (NS) stimuli for each mouse, we calculated a social distinction index

span.label: nonsocial odors
span.quote: The average unit tuning, calculated as the normalized odor-evoked response magnitude in all units that showed stimulus-associated responses, was higher for both male and female cues than for all nonsocial odors, regardless of odor identity

span.label: odor-evoked response magnitude
span.quote: The average unit tuning, calculated as the normalized odor-evoked response magnitude in all units that showed stimulus-associated responses, was higher for both male and female cues than for all nonsocial odors, regardless of odor identity

span.label: separation
span.quote: To quantify the separation between representation of social (S) and nonsocial (NS) stimuli for each mouse, we calculated a social distinction index

span.label: baseline noise levels
span.quote: Multiple regression analysis revealed that the elevated baseline noise levels in Cntnap2-/- mice could not be linearly predicted by either elevated baseline unit firing rates, nor by behavioral locomotion levels

span.label: a social stimulus, here - AN ODOUR FROM A CONSPECIFIC: the tuning measure is odor-evoked response magnitude, higher for male and female cues than for all nonsocial odors regardless of odor identity, so every 'social' difference reported is a difference between two sets of smells
span.quote: The average unit tuning, calculated as the normalized odor-evoked response magnitude in all units that showed stimulus-associated responses, was higher for both male and female cues than for all nonsocial odors, regardless of odor identity

span.label: the social distinction index - A LOG RATIO OF POPULATION DISTANCES: introduced to quantify the separation between social and nonsocial representations per mouse, so a phrase that reads as a faculty names a ratio between distances among activity patterns - and the paper prints the formula beside the name
span.quote: To quantify the separation between representation of social (S) and nonsocial (NS) stimuli for each mouse, we calculated a social distinction index

span.label: the behavioural evidence - ONE DIFFERENCE OUT OF THREE MEASURES: orientation probability was higher for social cues while response latency and locomotion increase did not significantly differ, so the animals' overt behaviour separates the categories on one axis and not on two
span.quote: The probability of odor-directed orientation responses was higher during delivery of social cues (Fig. 1c). However, the response latency (Fig. 1d) and the stimulus-evoked increase in locomotion (Fig. 1e) did not significantly differ between social and nonsocial stimuli

span.label: extends → prior work on experience-dependent divergence of conspecific sex representations in hypothalamus and medial amygdala
span.quote: These findings expand upon recent work describing experience-dependent divergence of conspecific sex representations in the hypothalamus76 and medial amygdala77.

span.label: builds-on → Lazaro et al., "Reduced prefrontal synaptic connectivity and disturbed oscillatory population dynamics in the CNTNAP2 model of autism" (bioRxiv 2018)
span.quote: Furthermore, recent work by Lazaro et al. (“Reduced prefrontal synaptic connectivity and disturbed oscillatory population dynamics in the CNTNAP2 model of autism”, bioRxiv 2018) demonstrates reduced dendritic spine and synapse densities in the mPFC of Cntnap2-/- mice, providing a potential mechanism for the functional impairments we describe.

span.label: separation —operationalised-as→ social distinction index
span.quote: To quantify the separation between representation of social (S) and nonsocial (NS) stimuli for each mouse, we calculated a social distinction index

span.label: Friedman test
span.quote: Friedman test for comparison of all stimuli,

span.label: Wilcoxon signed-rank test
span.quote: Friedman test with post hoc Wilcoxon signed-ranked test for social, nonsocial and clean air comparison,

span.label: ANOVA
span.quote: Two-way repeated measures (RM) ANOVA, Fphase(1,5) = 8.151, P < 0.05;

span.label: t-test
chi-squared
span.quote: For right panel: χ2 (5) = 21.182, P < 0.001.

span.label: standardized residuals
span.quote: Standardized residual analysis was used to determine significantly different response categories (|standardized residual| > 2).

span.label: z-score
span.quote: Response Z-score was calculated across repetitions per stimulus, per unit, and |Zscore| ≥ 2 threshold was used to determine responsive units and response specificity.

span.label: Bonferroni correction
span.quote: Superscript letters represent significant pairwise comparisons, determined by RM ANOVA with Bonferroni correction for post hoc comparisons.

span.label: Levene's test
span.quote: test was used to assess equality of variances, and statistical parameters were adjusted accordingly when needed.

span.label: principal component analysis
span.quote: First, we discretized neural responses into 150 ms bins, and used Principal Component Analysis (PCA) to project the population firing rates (FR) as a function of time, onto the first two principal components (see Online Methods).

span.label: cross-validation
span.quote: we fitted both a first- and a second-order model, and used the one that gave higher cross-validation values

span.label: multiple regression
span.quote: Multiple regression analysis revealed that the elevated baseline noise levels in Cntnap2-/- mice could not be linearly predicted by either elevated baseline unit firing rates, nor by behavioral locomotion levels (Supplementary Fig. 7c,d).

span.label: maximum likelihood classification
span.quote: To decode stimulus identity and stimulus category, we constructed maximum likelihood classifiers using encoding models of the entire population of simultaneously recorded units.

span.label: standard error of the mean
span.quote: Data is presented as mean ± SEM.

span.label: In the mouse medial prefrontal cortex, nearly a quarter of recorded units were selective for social odours, twice as many as were selective for nonsocial odours or showed mixed responses.
span.quote: Almost a quarter of recorded units displayed selectivity to social signals - twice the number of units with nonsocial odor selectivity or mixed social/nonsocial responses (Fig. 2c left and Supplementary Fig. 2c-e).

span.label: The mPFC population code is organised by social versus nonsocial category rather than by odour identity or valence: responses to the two social cues were more similar to each other than to any nonsocial odour.
span.quote: The block-diagonal structure of the dissimilarity matrix reflects a category-based organization of the population codebook in the mPFC: encoding distributions of the social cues were significantly more similar to each other than to any of the nonsocial odors, regardless of odor identity or valence (Fig. 3d).

span.label: Average unit tuning was stronger for both male and female social cues than for any of the three nonsocial odours, independent of odour identity.
span.quote: The average unit tuning, calculated as the normalized odor-evoked response magnitude in all units that showed stimulus-associated responses, was higher for both male and female cues than for all nonsocial odors, regardless of odor identity (Fig. 2e).

span.label: In wild-type mice the social distinction index rose significantly from the first to the second recording day, showing experience-dependent refinement of the social representation.
span.quote: The SDI values consistently and significantly increased between the first and second recording days for all wt mice.

span.label: Cntnap2 knockout mice showed no experience-dependent change: their social distinction index was unchanged between the two recording sessions.
span.quote: In contrast, no consistent change occurred in the Cntnap2-/- group, and mean SDI values in these mice remained unchanged between sessions (Fig. 4e).

span.label: The autism-model deficit is specific to categorisation rather than to stimulus encoding: single-odour decoding was equally accurate in both genotypes, but social/nonsocial category decoding was significantly worse in Cntnap2 knockouts.
span.quote: Remarkably, decoding performance for individual odors was similar in wt and Cntnap2-/- mice, whereas performance for odor category (S or NS) was significantly inferior in Cntnap2-/- mice (Fig. 5d).

span.label: Baseline (ongoing) population activity was noisier in Cntnap2 knockout mice than in wild-type littermates, with the two genotypes almost completely non-overlapping on this measure.
span.quote: We found that this measure of noise was significantly higher in Cntnap2-/- mice compared to their wt littermates (Fig. 6b-c; note that with the exception of one mouse, the noise measure of the two genotypes were completely non-overlapping).

span.label: Mean baseline firing rates of mPFC units were higher in Cntnap2 knockout mice than in wild-type littermates.
span.quote: Consistently, we found that the mean baseline firing rates of mPFC units recorded in Cntnap2-/- mice were significantly higher than those recorded in their wt littermates (Fig. 6a).

span.label: Across both genotypes, the level of baseline neuronal noise was strongly negatively correlated with the social distinction index.
span.quote: Remarkably, we found that across genotypes, baseline neuronal noise showed a strong negative correlation with SDI values (Fig. 6d).

span.label: Baseline cortical noise predicted how much a mouse's social representation refined with experience: higher noise went with a smaller day-to-day gain in the social distinction index.
span.quote: Strikingly, ΔSDI values in individual mice were strongly correlated with baseline cortical noise, such that elevated noise levels were predictive of decreased experience-dependent refinement of mPFC social representation (Fig. 6e).

span.label: The neural preference for social cues was not explained by behaviour: latency to orient and stimulus-evoked locomotion did not differ between social and nonsocial odours.
span.quote: However, the response latency (Fig. 1d) and the stimulus-evoked increase in locomotion (Fig. 1e) did not significantly differ between social and nonsocial stimuli.

span.label: social distinction index (SDI)
span.quote: Higher index values indicate greater divergence between social and nonsocial stimuli.

span.label: Jensen-Shannon divergence (as a representational distance)
span.quote: Jensen-Shannon divergence is a symmetrized version of the Kullbak-Leibler divergence, which measures in bits how distinguishable two distributions are, yielding 0 for identical distributions and 1 for non-overlapping distributions52.

span.label: cortical noise (baseline population variability)
span.quote: To evaluate cortical noise levels, we calculated the average fluctuations of population activity vectors during ongoing (baseline) activity before stimulus presentations:

span.label: unit tuning
span.quote: The average unit tuning, calculated as the normalized odor-evoked response magnitude in all units that showed stimulus-associated responses, was higher for both male and female cues than for all nonsocial odors, regardless of odor identity (Fig. 2e).

span.label: odour stimulus category (social male/female cues vs three nonsocial odours)
span.term: odour stimulus category (social male/female cues vs three nonsocial odours)
span.quote: Each mouse was repeatedly presented (in pseudorandomized order) with the odors of male mice (M), female mice (F), and with three nonsocial odors of distinct valence: banana extract (B), considered to be a neutral stimulus to mice48; peanut oil (P), an attractive stimulus48; and hexanal (H), known to be mildly repellent49.

span.label: genotype (Cntnap2 knockout vs wild-type littermate)
span.quote: We thus presented Cntnap2-/- mice with the same set of social and nonsocial stimuli, using their age-matched wildtype littermates as controls

span.label: prior experience with the odour set (recording session 1 vs session 2)
span.term: prior experience with the odour set (recording session 1 vs session 2)
span.quote: To characterize how population representations in the mPFC might undergo experience-dependent refinement, we compared neuronal responses to the stimuli in two consecutive recording sessions less than one week apart, for each mouse.

span.label: stimulus-evoked firing rate of mPFC units
span.term: stimulus-evoked firing rate of mPFC units
span.quote: To determine unit responsivity, evoked firing rates were calculated for the 5 seconds of stimulus presentation and compared to baseline firing rates during the preceding 5 seconds of baseline recordings.

span.label: baseline population activity noise
span.quote: To evaluate cortical noise levels, we calculated the average fluctuations of population activity vectors during ongoing (baseline) activity before stimulus presentations:

span.label: behavioural locomotion level
span.quote: Multiple regression analysis revealed that the elevated baseline noise levels in Cntnap2-/- mice could not be linearly predicted by either elevated baseline unit firing rates, nor by behavioral locomotion levels (Supplementary Fig. 7c,d).

span.label: n = 194 — number of mPFC single units recorded in the first cohort of six mice
span.quote: We recorded stimulus-evoked responses of mPFC units (n = 194; 6 mice) and found that 44% responded to at least one stimulus, typically by increasing their firing rates (Fig. 2a and Supplementary Fig. 2a-c).

span.label: 44% — proportion of recorded mPFC units that responded to at least one odour stimulus
span.quote: We recorded stimulus-evoked responses of mPFC units (n = 194; 6 mice) and found that 44% responded to at least one stimulus, typically by increasing their firing rates (Fig. 2a and Supplementary Fig. 2a-c).

span.label: 51% — proportion of responsive units that responded to only one specific stimulus
span.quote: Among responsive units, 51% were stimulus-specific, of which a large fraction responded exclusively to male or female cues (Fig. 2c, right).

span.label: from 44% on day 1 to 58% on day 2 — rise in the share of non-responsive units in Cntnap2 knockout mice across the two sessions
span.quote: Cntnap2-/- mice showed a similar decrease in the percentage of mixed-response units, but this was accompanied by an increase in the percentage of non-responsive units (from 44% on day 1 to 58% on day 2; Fig. 4a).

span.label: 269 / 237 — total units recorded in Cntnap2 knockout mice versus wild-type littermates across both days
span.quote: We recorded a total of 269 units in Cntnap2-/- mice (133 on day 1 and 136 on day 2) and 237 in wt littermates (125 on day 1 and 112 on day 2, Supplementary Fig. 4).

span.label: 75% — variance in population activity captured by the first two principal components in the example projection
span.quote: Here, the first two principal components accounted for 75% of the variance.

span.label: social = 98.33 ± 1.05, nonsocial = 87.22 ± 3.03, clean air = 65 ± 7.63 — mean probability of an odour-evoked orientation response by stimulus class
span.quote: (mean response probability: social = 98.33 ± 1.05, nonsocial = 87.22 ± 3.03, clean air = 65 ± 7.63)

span.label: t(103) = 3.285, P < 0.01 — test of the higher evoked response magnitude to social versus nonsocial stimuli
